question: Nursing is best described as a combination of which two elements?
explanation: Nursing blends the technical, evidence-based knowledge of science with the human, compassionate touch of art. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T1#BMP110_U1_T1_h1)

question: Why do modern nurses need formal academic training?

options.A: It replaces the need for practical experience in clinical wards
options.B: It equips practitioners to handle complex health technologies and evidence-based care
options.C: It focuses solely on passing licensing examinations
options.D: It allows nurses to manage hospital finances and administrative budgets

explanation: You've got this! Modern healthcare is fast-paced and relies on solid scientific understanding and problem-solving to keep patients safe every day. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T1#BMP110_U1_T1_h1)

question: What does 'autonomy' mean when we talk about nursing care?

options.A: Performing surgical procedures without prior authorization
options.B: Managing hospital supplies and pharmaceutical inventory
options.C: Working strictly under the direct supervision of a senior physician
options.D: Making independent nursing judgments within one's scope of practice

explanation: Think of autonomy as your professional superpower! It means making smart, independent clinical decisions and standing by your professional actions. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T1#BMP110_U1_T1_h2)

question: When a nurse provides holistic care, what are they focusing on?

options.A: The physical, mental, social, and spiritual needs of the patient
options.B: The administrative paperwork required for hospital discharge
options.C: The financial status and insurance coverage of the family
options.D: Only the specific disease process diagnosed by the doctor

explanation: Holistic care is all about seeing the whole human being sitting in front of you, not just their chart or their diagnosis! [learn more](BMP110_U1_T1#BMP110_U1_T1_h2)

question: Which organization is legally responsible for regulating nursing education and practice in Nigeria?

options.C: Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria

explanation: The NMCN is the statutory body charged with regulating nursing and midwifery standards in Nigeria. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T1#BMP110_U1_T1_h3)

question: What makes someone legally qualified to practice as a nurse in Nigeria?

options.A: Obtaining a recommendation letter from a senior medical doctor
options.B: Completing approved training and registering with the licensing council
options.D: Working in a government hospital for at least two years

explanation: To practice legally, you need to finish your accredited school program and get that all-important registration with the council. You're on your way there! [learn more](BMP110_U1_T1#BMP110_U1_T1_h3)

question: If you are teaching a patient with high blood pressure about healthy eating and lifestyle changes, which nursing role are you playing?
explanation: Spot on! Whenever you are helping a patient understand their body and health, you are stepping proudly into your educator shoes. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T1#BMP110_U1_T1_h4)

question: Why is it important for a nurse to act as a patient advocate?

options.A: To protect patient rights and ensure they are well-informed about care
options.B: To manage the financial billing of hospital services
options.C: To enforce strict hospital visitation rules without exception
options.D: To make all medical and surgical decisions on behalf of the family

explanation: As an advocate, you are the patient's voice when they feel overwhelmed, making sure their rights and safety always come first. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T1#BMP110_U1_T1_h4)

question: Who introduced the earliest forms of formal Western nursing training in Nigeria?
explanation: History check! Christian missions laid the early groundwork by setting up the first formal hospitals and nurse training programs in Nigeria. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T1#BMP110_U1_T1_h5)

question: How has nursing in Nigeria grown from its early days to now?

options.A: It has shifted away from hospital care entirely toward office work
options.B: It has become exclusively focused on international recruitment
options.C: It has evolved from basic missionary training into structured professional diploma and degree programs
options.D: It has replaced traditional medicine completely without local influence

explanation: Look how far we've come! Nigerian nursing has grown into a well-structured profession with fantastic diploma and degree pathways. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T1#BMP110_U1_T1_h5)
